statistics.treatment: not built (pilot failed twice; no treatment statistic exists)

criterion_as_applied: Pilot (PREREG round 2): positive = C=16 pooled success fraction >=0.8 at p=1..4; cheat = full success criterion (p_max nondecreasing, p_max(8)-p_max(1)>=3, twin <=0.1 at all p>=2) met on injected grid; null twin meets success iff part A holds on its grid OR its fraction >0.1 at some p>=2 (NOTES A9). Fractions pooled over 5 seeds x 50 trials.

stupid_explanations_status.delta too small for longer orbits (repea: NOT TESTED (no treatment run; only relevant to treatment)
stupid_explanations_status.long-period UPOs located inaccurately: RULED OUT for the pilot: orbit residual abs(f^p(x)-x) <= 5.5e-14 for p=1..8
stupid_explanations_status.trajectory lands near the orbit by luck: RULED OUT as the source of null-twin success: uncontrolled trajectories reached 0 successes in 5 seeds x 8 x 8 x 50 lanes (cheat twin); null-twin successes come in whole 50/50 seed-cells, i.e. a stabilising gain, not luck

anomalies: Null twin never shows the memory law (p_max=0 at every C in both attempts) but a shuffled-fit controller stabilises whole cells (50/50 trials) in single seeds: a random proportional gain lands in the finite stabilising interval of a 1-D UPO. Pooled null fraction exceeded the spec's 0.1 twin bound at p>=2 in both attempts (0.2, then 0.4 after the intercept repair).
Spec's control and null_twin are the same construction (time-shuffled fit); both would be affected.

Positive control at C=16 already reached 1.0 at p=1..4; with a 1-D map a C=1 deadbeat controller is sufficient in principle (M5's own simpler_alternative: observability needs depth >= system order = 1). Not measured: no treatment run.
notes: Pilot attempt 1 failed on the null twin; one repair (fit with intercept, intercept dropped from controller; NOTES.md) and rerun; attempt 2 failed on the null twin again -> SPEC_UNATTAINABLE per PREREG round 2. No treatment code written. core_minutes = summed process time of pilot rows + ~0.2 min for UPO checks/evaluators.
